newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen up on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday rebounded after a one-day dip and analysts said more rises were likely on Thursday, in part because Tuesday's Funds rate rise in the United States had already been discounted by the market.
"(U.S. Fed Chairman Alan) Greenspan did what he did and it (the rate rise) was already priced in," said Bogdan Kornacki, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage.

Analysts said the market had put its recent deeper downward correction behind it and that some large-cap firms such as industrial and trading Elektrim might lead moderate market growth after recent falls.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.2 percent to 16,354.8 points and turnover rose 23 percent to 227.4 million zlotys ($73.7 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 67 to 12 with 14 stocks stable.

Four small-cap stocks rose between 8.7 and 9.9 percent on Wednesday, including debt-ridden Espebepe, which continued this week's speculative surge after last week's drop. The builder's creditors meet on April 14 to discuss a possible debt deal.
Cable maker Kable and builder Prochem were both up 9.9 percent, builder Mostostal Zabrze 8.7 percent, extending gains after news of a likely contract with Germany's Adam Opel AG.

Polifarb Cieszyn surged 9.5 percent and Polifarb Wroclaw fell 7.9 percent after the paintmakers' shareholders agreed on a merger earlier this week, with Cieszyn shareholders approving a plan giving them 53.5 percent
Wroclaw officials have said a mutual shareholder, bank BIG SA might dispute Cieszyn's version in court but that the merger was still likely to go through as a delay would cost both firms.
